pr_title: Avoid booting in development then test for test tasks
pr_body:
### Summary

Since #41132, we fork to run the tests from the test Rake tasks, which allows the tests to run when the task runs (previously it was only loading the tests, they ran at the process exit, which isn't helpful for rake tasks where you want to stop processing if a task dependency fails).

That means the app boots twice, first from the top of the Rakefile:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b7c3b52ce530d9914717ceafc64990a225ad96c4/railties/lib/rails/generators/rails/app/templates/Rakefile.tt#L4
then in the fork that runs the test runner.

It's not ideal but it is the only way to run tests in a Rake task since they run at exit.

But that caused some weird behavior/bugs like #43937 since the application boots in development first to load the tasks and then forks to run the tests. We had mentioned some potential problems where the global state in Ruby changed from the Rakefile wouldn't be available to the test process, but we missed the opposite, where an environment variable would be set in development and then available in the child process in the test environment.

> #41132 This diverges from previous behavior because now, any changes made in the Rakefile or other code loaded by Rake won't be available to the child process.

But investigating this, I realized we could define the test tasks as Thor tasks, which take priority over Rake tasks.

We keep the Rake tasks for compatibility (`rake test:models` will continue to work), but `rails test:models` won't go through Rake anymore. 

I built it on 7-0-stable because I think it's a regression that we want to fix, but let me know if you'd rather push that as a feature for 7.1 on main.

### Other Information

There is some incompatibility as mentioned in the commit where we could run `rails test:models ARG=value --trace` but now it won't work.

Another important point is that the `test:prepare` hook won't run when it used to. If you had this in your Rakefile:
```ruby
Rake::Task['test:prepare'].enhance { puts "test:prepare enhancement" }
```

… it would run with `rails test:models` but not with `rails test`. I haven't found any mention of the `test:prepare` hook in guides or documentation so I'll look into deprecating it ([rspec calls it](https://github.com/rspec/rspec-rails/blob/v5.0.2/lib/rspec/rails/tasks/rspec.rake#L25-L26) but doesn't enhance it).

For both cases, I think it's fair since the same wouldn't work with the test task (`rails test ARG=value --trace` fails and `rails test` doesn't run the `test:prepare` task either since it's not a Rake task).

Fixes #43937
pr_comments: PRs always open against `main`, unless the code is only necessary in a specific branch, which is not the case here.

We had an issue with some system tests that were failing due to the double booting (it seems to cause big issues with `Aws::STS`). Just wanted to confirm that this PR removed the double boot and fixed our issues 😍
Apart from the merge conflict is there anything else needed for this PR to be merged? It would be an awesome bug to have fixed on main. I am happy to help if needed.

Getting this merged would be highly appreciated! Last week another colleague lost the data in his `development` DB when running `rails test` because the wrong database configuration was used and he forgot to explicitly specify `RAILS_ENV=test`.

> when running `rails test`

That part is strange because `rails test` is already not booting twice, it's a Thor command, so the Rakefile is not involved.

> > when running `rails test`
> 
> That part is strange because `rails test` is already not booting twice, it's a Thor command, so the Rakefile is not involved.

Oops... :thinking: After encountering the issue the first time, I did an issue search and found this one. As it describes some effects extremely similar to what we have been observing (Rails using the `development` DB when running `rails test` but working fine when running `RAILS_ENV=test rails test`), I was under the impression that this would fix things.

As such I was hopeful that our issue would be resolved soon and did not look into it any closer. But if it's more likely to be something else, I'll investigate further. Thanks for the heads-up!
I can't speak for `rails test`, but we had similar issues on `rails test:system` and this PR definitely fixes that for us.
Any hope of this making it to 7.0? Most of my team had our development databases wiped out until we realized this regression existed.
No. 7.0 doesn't receive bug fixes anymore.

issue_context.title: Rails.env == "development" when starting system tests
issue_context.body:
When launching system tests, `Rails.env == "development"` after launching the tests, but is correctly `test` in the test themselves.

This is breaking thinks like the `dotenv-rails` gem, due to the following:
- `rails test:system` is started
- App is loaded, `Rails.env == "development"`, so `dotenv-rails` loads the env variables for `development`, and those are added to the process's `ENV` variable
- The main process then launches the tests's process, which inherits its parent's `ENV`
- `dotenv-rails` load the env variables for `test`
- But is some variables were set for `development` but dont have a value in `test`, they are still defined in the tests

### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->

- Create a new Rails 7 application
- Add `puts "Rails.env: #{Rails.env}"` to `config/application.rb` on line 7 (after the `Bundler.require` line)
- Run system tests: `rails test:system`

### Expected behavior
`Rails.env` should be `test`, as it is in Rails 6.1 and when running `rails test`

### Actual behavior
`Rails.env` is `development`

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
7.0.0
**Ruby version**:
3.0.3
comments:
I am not sure if this is related, but we are seeing another behaviour changes regarding ENV variables and tests:

In `test/test_helper.rb` we had the following:

```rb
require File.expand_path('../config/environment', __dir__)
require 'rails/test_help'

ENV['MYVAR'] = 'something'

class ActiveSupport::TestCase
  fixtures :all
 …
end
```

And in fixtures, we were using `ENV['MYVAR']`.

Starting with Rails 7, the ENV variable is undefined when loading the fixtures.

If `ENV['MYVAR'] = 'something'` is moved before loading `config/environment` then it is properly defined.

I confirm I have the same issue. I'm using dotenv-rails as well.

When launching system tests using `rails test:system` I have the same error.
If lauching using `rails test test/system/foo_test.rb` it uses the correct database.
Since you have a way to reproduce can you check what changed this behavior in Rails using git bisect?

I made a quick script that creates a new rails app and checks `Rails.env` after the bundle load in `config/application.rb` and used it to run a bisection.

The culprit seems to be #41298 with #41314 as a related commit.

cc @etiennebarrie

Since #41132 we create a fork to run the tests, which results in the app being loaded twice, and since #41298 like you mentioned, we don't automatically set `RAILS_ENV` to `"test"` for the tasks `default`, `test`, and those starting with `test:` like `test:system`, so this bug also applies to `test:models` .

I really think we should keep #41298 because it's pretty unclean to change the environment behind your back while loading a framework/library.

As a workaround, you can add a similar piece of code at the top of your Rakefile to get the same result:

```ruby
if Rake.application.top_level_tasks.grep(/^(default$|test(:|$))/).any?
  ENV["RAILS_ENV"] ||= Rake.application.options.show_tasks ? "development" : "test"
end
```

---

> Starting with Rails 7, the ENV variable is undefined when loading the fixtures.

I can't reproduce this. With a `bin/rails g scaffold account name`, then I add this:

<details><summary>Diff</summary>

```diff

```
</details>

And I run `bin/rails test:models`, I see that the app boots in development, then the fork in test, but the fixture uses the environment variable as expected. Running rails `db:fixtures:load` does not use the environment variable but that's expected since it loads the fixtures in development, without loading `test/test_helper.rb`:

```
$ bin/rails db:fixtures:load
{:rails_env=>"development"}
$ bin/rails runner 'puts Account.pluck(:name)'
{:rails_env=>"development"}
MyString
MyString
```

Same with `RAILS_ENV=test`, the test helper is not loaded for this:

```
$ RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:fixtures:load
{:rails_env=>"test"}                                 
$ bin/rails runner -e test 'puts Account.pluck(:name)'                                                                                                                                                                                               
{:rails_env=>"test"}                                 
MyString
MyString
```

But even then, running the tests, then running that again, the fixtures have the environment variable included.

Something I noticed with your setup though:

> In `test/test_helper.rb` we had the following:
> 
> ```ruby
> require File.expand_path('../config/environment', __dir__)
> ```

Since Rails 5.1.5 there is a line that sets the `RAILS_ENV` at the beginning of `test/test_helper.rb`:

 ```ruby
ENV['RAILS_ENV'] ||= 'test'
require File.expand_path('../config/environment', __dir__)
```

But even removing it on my machine, I still get the fixture loaded with the environment variable, so that's not the issue.

I added https://github.com/bkeepers/dotenv/pull/441 to fix dotenv-rails to set the environment when using Rake, but I also thought about it more and created #44106 here so that we don't do the double boot and fork if you use `rails test:system`, only if you use `rake test:system`.

Eventually arrived here after hours of head scratching. Here's a workaround that worked for me (based on https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/44106):

Append this code to the `config/boot.rb`:
```ruby
require_relative '../lib/rails/command/test_command' if [nil, 'test'].include?(ENV['RAILS_ENV'])
```

And then monkey patch rails test command (add `lib/rails/command/test_command.rb`):
```ruby
require 'rails/commands/test/test_command'

module Rails
  module Command
    class TestCommand < Base
      %i[models helpers channels controllers mailers integration jobs mailboxes system].each do |name|
        define_method(name) do |*|
          self.args = ["test/#{name}"]
          perform
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
```

I think the first snippet from https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/43937#issuecomment-1007288285 makes more sense. It's what was happening before, and it doesn't involve patching Rails. You just set the `RAILS_ENV` to test if the rake task is `default` or starts with `test` or `test:` (unless you're just listing the tasks with `rake -T`/`-D`/`-W` for some reason).

> I think the first snippet from [#43937 (comment)](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/43937#issuecomment-1007288285) makes more sense. It's what was happening before, and it doesn't involve patching Rails. You just set the `RAILS_ENV` to test if the rake task is `default` or starts with `test` or `test:` (unless you're just listing the tasks with `rake -T`/`-D`/`-W` for some reason).

There's another problem that this fix does not address (but the [above](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/43937#issuecomment-1099190349) one does): the application loads twice. Once in the current process and once more when falling through to the test rake task:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/c9e5057de4be7e0f4365ff9c2d411cffc39c3746/railties/lib/rails/test_unit/runner.rb#L35

Double load means twice as long startup time. Startup time is important.
Yeah I don't disagree. I should have thought of the solution I found in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/44106 in the first place.
